title: Insurance Claim Services Standing Rule: One Claim File and One Deductible per Occurrence
content:
**Standing rule.** No other claim file that is not withdrawn may exist for the same carrier name and carrier claim number. Every job the company performs for the same loss, whether water, fire or mold mitigation, the rebuild contract or contents packout, is linked to that one claim file, because the carrier adjusts one claim per occurrence. The deductible is one per occurrence: it is assessed once on the claim file, however many jobs the loss produces, and it is never charged on a job.

This Insurance Claim Services rule applies when a claim file is opened and when a deductible is assessed.

## The duplicate check when a file is opened

- The check rests on the system's records, before the file is opened: the carrier name together with the carrier claim number of the file being opened are compared with the claim files already on record.
- A claim file on record for the same carrier name and carrier claim number blocks the new file when its status is opened, estimate submitted, approved, settled, closed or denied.
- A withdrawn file for the same carrier name and carrier claim number does not block a new file.

| Existing file for the same carrier and claim number | New file may be opened? |
|---|---|
| none | yes |
| withdrawn | yes |
| opened, estimate submitted, approved, settled, closed or denied | no |

## Jobs and the deductible

- Water, fire and mold mitigation jobs, the rebuild contract and the contents packout job of the same loss are all linked to the one claim file.
- The deductible is assessed once on the claim file, never on a job, however many jobs the loss produces.

*Example (hypothetical):* a loss produces a water mitigation job, a contents packout job and later a rebuild contract. All three are linked to the single claim file for that carrier claim, and one deductible is assessed on the file.
